html:
SMTO-EXE-0234 — The Docker image build failed

GUID: bb1c1c84-8379-5eb6-ae68-1aee917e32d8
Slug: docker-build-failed
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: docker

What happened

  • Docker started building the image on the Gateway computer but reported an error partway through. Some steps may have finished and left files or tags behind, but the image you asked for wasn't confirmed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to list the Docker images on that Gateway, to see whether an image with your tag was created or changed anyway. The build may have got far enough to create or retag an image even though it reported failure.
  2. Ask the person who manages that computer to run the same build in the project folder there; Docker shows which step failed and why. SMTO doesn't pass on Docker's full build messages, because they can contain passwords or other secrets.
  3. Fix the cause in the build recipe (the Dockerfile) or the project files, such as a missing file or a failed install step, then ask SMTO to build again. Building again without a fix will hit the same error.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the build finished, and the new image appears in the image list with your tag.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the project folder location, to the person who manages Docker on that computer. Don't delete leftover images or build files until they've checked what the failed build left behind.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An image_build or compose_build reported an operation failure after the build reached the Docker Engine, and the follow-up check did not confirm a successful image; partial layers, cache or tags may remain.

What this means

  • After mutation began, a build returned an operation-failed error and existing reconciliation did not establish success. Partial image/cache/tag effects may remain. Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.

Why this can happen

  • After mutation began, a build returned an operation-failed error and existing reconciliation did not establish success. Partial image/cache/tag effects may remain.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect bounded build progress, known_completed facts and exact image/cache state on the selected Engine.

How to fix it

  • Docker error bodies are not relayed, so reproduce the build on the Gateway host as the Gateway account (docker build, or docker compose build, with the same context, Dockerfile, build arguments and tag) to read the failing step. Inspect images, tags and build cache for partial effects of the original attempt, fix the cause, then submit a new build; never replay it automatically.
  • Inspect retained build evidence and partial Engine state, then correct the actual build failure before deciding on new work.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the exact object identity, typed arguments and selected Gateway capability; correct the reported prerequisite before a new request.

How to verify the fix

  • Original build effects are understood and a corrected authorized build completes with a verified image identity.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain Docker mutation.

Technical notes

  • Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
